questions.title: Mathematical Literacy Terms, True/False Statements, and World Temperatures

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term or concept in COLUMN A. Write only the letter (A–I). 1.1.1 Ratio scale
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: I (number scale)
Mark 1: Identifying that a ratio scale is expressed as a number scale.
Mark 2: Correct letter selection (I).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term or concept in COLUMN A. 1.1.2 Grams in one ton
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 000 000)
Mark 1: Recognising that 1 ton = 1 000 000 grams.
Mark 2: Correct letter selection (B).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term or concept in COLUMN A. 1.1.3 Surface area of a cylinder
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: H ($2 \times \pi \times \text{radius}^2 + 2 \times \pi \times \text{radius} \times \text{height}$)
Mark 1: Identifying the correct formula for the surface area of a cylinder.
Mark 2: Correct letter selection (H).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches the term or concept in COLUMN A. 1.1.4 Floor plan
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: G (plan that shows the layout of a building, as seen from above)
Mark 1: Recognising that a floor plan is a top-down view of a building.
Mark 2: Correct letter selection (G).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets to make the statement TRUE: A probability is always (less than/greater than) or equal to one.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: less than
Mark 1: Understanding that probability ranges from 0 to 1.
Mark 2: Correct word selection (less than).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets to make the statement TRUE: When calculating the amount of medicine to administer to a toddler, we round (up/down) the decimal answer, in millilitres.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: down
Mark 1: Understanding that medicine doses for toddlers must be rounded down to avoid overdose.
Mark 2: Correct word selection (down).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets to make the statement TRUE: A flow rate of 12,5 litres/hour is equal to 25 litres in (two/three) hours.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: two
Mark 1: Calculating $12{,}5 \times 2 = 25$ litres.
Mark 2: Correct word selection (two).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets to make the statement TRUE: An elevation plan of a building is a (2D/3D) representation of the building.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 2D
Mark 1: Understanding that an elevation plan is a flat, two-dimensional representation showing one side of a building.
Mark 2: Correct word selection (2D).
[Award 2 marks for the correct choice]

subQuestions.questionText: The picture shows the 10 hottest and the 10 coldest countries in the world, based on their average temperature over time. Write down the average temperature in Sweden. (Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 1,75 °C
Mark 1: Reading the value from the diagram.
Mark 2: Correct value with appropriate unit (no penalty for omitting unit).
[Award 2 marks for correct reading]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the third hottest country.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Kiribati
Mark 1: Identifying that Burkina Faso (28,29°C) is hottest, Mali (28,25°C) is second, Kiribati (28,20°C) is third.
Mark 2: Correct country name.
[Award 2 marks for correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Round off Russia's average temperature to the nearest °C.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading Russia's average temperature: $-5{,}35°C$
Mark 2: Correct rounding to nearest °C: $\approx -5°C$
[NPU – No penalty for omitting unit]
[Award 2 marks: 1 for the correct temperature read, 1 for correct rounding]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the difference between the average temperatures of Senegal and Iceland.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct temperatures (Senegal = 27,85°C; Iceland = –0,70°C).
Mark 2: Subtracting –0,70°C from 27,85°C: $\text{Difference} = 27{,}85°C - (-0{,}70°C)$
Mark 3: Simplification: $= 28{,}55°C$
Accept –28,55°C
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the names of ALL the countries that have the exact same temperatures.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer:
• Djibouti and Mauritius (both 28,00°C)
• Mauritania and Tuvali/Tuvalu (both 27,65°C)
Mark 1–2: First correct pair (Djibouti and Mauritius).
Mark 3: Second correct pair (Mauritania and Tuvali).
[Award 3 marks: 2 for the first correct pair and 1 for the second correct pair]

questions.title: Supermarket Layout Plan and Customer Data

subQuestions.questionText: Clive followed the directions below to buy an item from this supermarket: Enter the supermarket and immediately turn right. Walk past the magazine section and then turn left. Continue straight ahead until you come to the end of the aisle. The item will be in the section on your right. Name the type of product Clive bought. (Refer to ANNEXURE A in the answer book showing the supermarket layout plan.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Cleaning supplies
Mark 1: Following the directions correctly on the layout plan.
Mark 2: Correct identification of the product section.
[Award 2 marks for the correct product]

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the location of the pet care section.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Pet care is next to the sweets, just to the left of the checkout points. (Or: Between sweets and checkout point / Last section before checkout point.)
Mark 1: Explanation with the first reference (e.g., next to sweets).
Mark 2: Explanation with the second reference (e.g., left of checkout / before checkout point).
[Award 2 marks for a complete location description with two reference points]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the section where you will find milk and yoghurt.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Dairy and cheese
Mark 1–2: Correct section identified.
[Award 2 marks for the correct section]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word from those given in brackets to make the following statement TRUE: The customer flow of the supermarket, as displayed in the layout plan, is (clockwise/anti-clockwise).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: anti-clockwise
Mark 1–2: Correct option selected based on the layout plan flow direction.
[Award 2 marks for the correct option]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE positive impact that a properly labelled section and an attractive set-up in a supermarket will have on a customer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following:
• Encourages customers to make purchases.
• Pleasant environment – customers like to shop there.
• To encourage customers to return to shop again.
• Easy to find items / easy access / convenience.
• User friendly.
• Save time.
[Award 2 marks for a valid reason]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE possible reason why the cool drinks, butchery, dairy and cheese sections are located against the back wall of the supermarket.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following:
• Fridges need power/plugs to run.
• Safety – the wires do not trip the customers.
• Easy to pack.
• Temperature control.
• To have all the cold products lined up in one row.
[Award 2 marks for a valid reason]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a possible name for the symbol [T] in the layout plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Acceptable answers:
• Tills
• Cashiers
• It is the place where you need to pay (checkout/till point).
[Award 2 marks for any correct identification of the symbol]

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 2 records the gender of customers and the colours of outfits as customers entered the supermarket. Some values have been omitted (a, b, c, d). Calculate the missing values a, b, c and d. The table shows: Female row: BLACK = a, RED = 31, BLUE = 10, GREEN = 16, BROWN = 9, YELLOW = 4, TOTAL = c. Male row: BLACK = 25, RED = 7, BLUE = b, GREEN = 13, BROWN = 9, YELLOW = 2, TOTAL = 68. TOTAL row: BLACK = 43, RED = 38, BLUE = 22, GREEN = 29, BROWN = 18, YELLOW = 6, TOTAL = d.
Determine the probability of randomly selecting a female from the people wearing green outfits.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Numerator – number of females wearing green = 16
Mark 2: Denominator – total people wearing green = 29
$P = \dfrac{16}{29} \approx 0{,}55 \approx 55{,}17\%$
[NPR – No penalty for rounding if first decimal is correct]
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Clive wrote down the following probability as a possible outcome: P(outcome) = $\dfrac{25}{68}$. Give the gender and the colour of the outfit represented by this probability.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Identifying gender as Male (since the denominator 68 = total males).
Mark 3: Identifying colour as Black (since 25 males wore black).
Answer: Male and Black
[Award 3 marks: 2 for first part (Male) and 1 for second part (Black)]

questions.title: Garden Plan, Fishpond, Paving and Costing

subQuestions.questionText: A garden landscaper is helping Mrs Mbele to plan a garden behind her house. There will be paving bricks laid between the house and the garden. The front of the garden will have the house as one of its boundaries, while the rest of the outer boundaries of the garden will have wire fencing. Calculate the total length of the wire fencing needed to fence the outer boundaries of the garden, including the paved area. (Refer to ANNEXURE B in the answer book showing the plan for the proposed garden.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Adding all the values: $12 \text{ m} + 8{,}7 \text{ m} + 2{,}6 \text{ m} + 12 \text{ m}$
Mark 2: Simplification: $= 35{,}3 \text{ m}$
Mark 3: Correct unit (m).
OR alternative: $12 \text{ m} + 8{,}7 \text{ m} + 2{,}6 \text{ m} + 1{,}4 \text{ m} + 10{,}6 \text{ m} = 35{,}3 \text{ m}$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.1.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The circular fishpond (A) has a diameter of 120 cm and a depth of 0,5 m. Calculate, in cm³, the volume of the fishpond. Use the formula: Volume of the cylinder = $3{,}142 \times \text{radius}^2 \times \text{depth}$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Radius = $120 \div 2 = 60$ cm
Mark 2: Substitution: $V = 3{,}142 \times (60 \text{ cm})^2 \times \text{depth}$
Mark 3: Conversion m to cm: $0{,}5 \text{ m} = 50 \text{ cm}$
Mark 4: Simplification: $V = 3{,}142 \times 3600 \times 50 = 565{,}560 \text{ cm}^3$
$$V = 565{,}560 \text{ cm}^3$$
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.1.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Surrounding the circumference of the fishpond is a row of paving bricks. Each paving brick is 20 cm long. Determine the circumference of the paved outer edging of the fishpond. Use the formula: Circumference of a circle = $3{,}142 \times \text{diameter}$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Adding 20 cm to both sides: Diameter $= 120 \text{ cm} + (2 \times 20 \text{ cm}) = 160 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Substitution: $C = 3{,}142 \times 160 \text{ cm}$
Mark 3: Simplification: $C = 502{,}72 \text{ cm}$
OR
Mark 1: New radius $= 60 \text{ cm} + 20 \text{ cm} = 80 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Substitution: $C = 3{,}142 \times 2 \times 80 \text{ cm}$
Mark 3: Simplification: $C = 502{,}72 \text{ cm}$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The rectangular paved area (C on the plan) between the garden and the house is 36,16 m². Calculate the width of the paved area between the garden and the house. Use the formula: Area of a rectangle = length × width
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Length = $8{,}7 \text{ m} + 2{,}6 \text{ m} = 11{,}3 \text{ m}$
Mark 2: Substitution: $36{,}16 \text{ m}^2 = 11{,}3 \text{ m} \times \text{width}$
Mark 3: Changing the subject: $\text{width} = \dfrac{36{,}16 \text{ m}^2}{11{,}3 \text{ m}}$
Mark 4: Simplification: $\text{width} = 3{,}2 \text{ m}$
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: 118 wheelbarrows of gravel are needed for 10 m³ of gravel. Thabang stated that more than 65 wheelbarrows of gravel are needed to place a 150 mm layer of gravel under the paved area. Verify, with calculations, whether his statement is VALID. Use the formula: Volume of rectangular prism = Area of rectangle × depth
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution: $V = 36{,}16 \text{ m}^2 \times 150 \text{ mm}$
Mark 2: Conversion mm to m: $150 \text{ mm} = 0{,}150 \text{ m}$
Mark 3: Simplification: $V = 36{,}16 \text{ m}^2 \times 0{,}150 \text{ m} = 5{,}424 \text{ m}^3$
Mark 4: Using ratio: 10 m³ requires 118 wheelbarrows, so 5,424 m³ requires $n = \dfrac{5{,}424 \times 118}{10}$
Mark 5: Simplification: $n \approx 64{,}0 \approx 65$ wheelbarrows (Accept 64)
Mark 6: Conclusion: Statement is INVALID (since exactly 65 — not more than 65 — wheelbarrows are needed; or 64, depending on rounding).
[Award 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The paved seating area (B on the plan), alongside, is located at the eastern side of the garden. This area has a circular paving brick in the middle, surrounded by custom-made pavers (irregularly shaped paving bricks) to form the circular paved seating area. The custom-made pavers are sold in packs of 13, which covers exactly a quarter of the full circular seating area, excluding the middle paver. Determine the total number of paving bricks in the first row, closest to the middle circular paver. (Refer to the picture of the layout of the circular paved area in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 12
Mark 1–2: From the picture, the first row (innermost ring around the centre paver) contains 12 paving bricks (3 bricks per quarter × 4 quarters = 12).
[Award 2 marks for the correct number]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total cost, including VAT, of the materials required to pave the entire seating area B. Costs (excluding 15% VAT): Middle paver = R125,80; Pack of 13 custom-made pavers = R657,40; Other materials = R1 250,00.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Adding three costs (multiplying pack by 4 to cover full circle): $\text{Total (excl VAT)} = \text{R}125{,}80 + 4 \times \text{R}657{,}40 + \text{R}1\,250{,}00$
Mark 2: Multiplying by 4: $4 \times \text{R}657{,}40 = \text{R}2\,629{,}60$
Mark 3: Simplification: $= \text{R}4\,005{,}40$
Mark 4: VAT calculation: $\text{VAT} = \text{R}4\,005{,}40 \times 15\% = \text{R}600{,}81$
Mark 5: Total (incl VAT) = $\text{R}4\,005{,}40 + \text{R}600{,}81 = \text{R}4\,606{,}21$
OR
$\text{R}4\,005{,}40 \times 1{,}15 = \text{R}4\,606{,}21$
[Award 5 marks]

questions.title: Pet Shop, Mini Aquariums and Wall Arrangement

subQuestions.questionText: Nikita wants to open her own pet shop. She will sell fish tanks in the shape of mini aquarium blocks. Inner length = 11,6 cm; Inner width = 7,6 cm; Inner height = 10,5 cm; 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ. Determine (in simplified form) the ratio of the length to the width of the mini aquarium block tank.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct values – $11{,}6 : 7{,}6$
Mark 2: Correct order (length : width).
Mark 3: Simplification – $11{,}6 : 7{,}6 = 29 : 19$ (multiplying both sides by 2,5 / dividing by HCF)
[Answer Only acceptable for full marks]
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The operating hours of the pet shop are: Monday to Friday 07:30 to 17:00; Saturday 08:00 to 13:00; Sunday Closed. Calculate the total number of hours the pet shop will be open in one operating week.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Hours per day Mon–Fri: $17{:}00 - 07{:}30 = 9$ hours $30$ min
Mark 2: Multiplying by 5 days: $9{,}5 \times 5$
Mark 3: Time for 5 days: $= 47{,}5$ hours
Mark 4: Time for Saturday: $13{:}00 - 08{:}00 = 5$ hours
Mark 5: Simplification: Total time $= 47{,}5 + 5 = 52{,}5$ hours
[Award 5 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Each mini aquarium tank will contain 75% of its capacity in water. Determine the amount of water left over in a jug (1 000 mℓ), after filling one mini aquarium tank with water. Use the formula: Volume = length × width × height
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution: $V = 11{,}6 \text{ cm} \times 7{,}6 \text{ cm} \times 10{,}5 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Simplification: $V = 925{,}68 \text{ cm}^3$
Mark 3: Capacity in mℓ: $1 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ m}\ell$, so $925{,}68 \text{ cm}^3 = 925{,}68 \text{ m}\ell$
Mark 4: Calculating 75% of tank: $925{,}68 \times 75\%$
Mark 5: Simplification: $= 694{,}26 \text{ m}\ell$
Mark 6: Subtracting from 1000 mℓ: $1\,000 \text{ m}\ell - 694{,}26 \text{ m}\ell$
Mark 7: mℓ left: $= 305{,}74 \text{ m}\ell$
[Award 7 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a picture (A, B, C, D, E or F) that will match the written instruction: Place the outer frame over the transparent inner to cover it. (Refer to the assembly pictures in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D
Mark 1: Correct letter selection.
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a picture that will match the written instruction: Pull in opposite directions to open the mini aquarium.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A
Mark 1: Correct letter selection.
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a picture that will match the written instruction: The hole is for feeding or to put in a light.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: F
Mark 1: Correct letter selection.
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a picture that will match the written instruction: One hand will hold the transparent inner tank while the other hand will hold the outer frame.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B
Mark 1: Correct letter selection.
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a picture that will match the written instruction: Add water and decorating items as you like.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C
Mark 1: Correct letter selection.
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a picture that will match the written instruction: Close tightly by pressing down on the outer frame.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: E
Mark 1: Correct letter selection.
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Nikita decided to assemble a few of the mini aquariums and mount them against the wall at the front desk. The outer length = 12 cm, outer width = 8 cm, outer height = 4,3 inches. NOTE: 1 mm = 0,0394 inches. Determine, in cm, the height of one mini aquarium tank.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct height in inches: $4{,}3$ inches
Mark 2: Dividing by 0,0394: $\text{Height} = \dfrac{4{,}3 \text{ inches}}{0{,}0394 \text{ inches/mm}}$
Mark 3: Simplification in mm: $= 109{,}1370558 \text{ mm}$
Mark 4: Conversion from mm to cm: $= 10{,}9 \text{ cm}$ (or 10,914 cm or 10,91 cm)
[NPR – No penalty for rounding if first decimal is correct]
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: There is a 5 cm space between each mini aquarium tank along the length of the wall. In every odd row, the mini aquarium tanks start and end against the wall. Wall length = 199 cm; Wall height = 100 cm. Calculate the total number of mini aquarium tanks Nikita will be able to place in the bottom row to maximise the space along the length of the wall.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Adding length and space: One tank + space = $12 \text{ cm} + 5 \text{ cm} = 17 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Simplification (number lengthwise): $199 \div 17 = 11{,}70588... \approx 11$
Mark 3: Dividing: Calculate full units that fit.
Mark 4: Simplification: $17 \times 11 = 187 \text{ cm}$
Mark 5: Calculating space left: $199 - 187 = 12 \text{ cm}$
Mark 6: Simplification: One additional tank fits in the remaining 12 cm (no space needed at end).
Mark 7: Final answer: $11 + 1 = 12$ mini aquariums
OR alternative method:
Mark 1: Tank + space = $12 + 5 = 17 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Place 2 tanks at the ends: $12 + 12 = 24 \text{ cm}$
Mark 3: Two tanks and 1 space: $24 + 5 = 29 \text{ cm}$
Mark 4: Space left: $199 - 29 = 170 \text{ cm}$
Mark 5: Use of space left: $170 \div 17 = 10$ tanks
Mark 6: Total tanks: $2 + 10 = 12$
Mark 7: Final consistent answer.
[Award 7 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: In the even rows, the mini aquarium tanks start at space d from the wall, on either side of the row. Nikita stated that length d is 8,5 cm. Verify, showing ALL calculations, if her statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Subtracting values: $12 \text{ cm} - 5 \text{ cm} = 7 \text{ cm}$ (length of 2nd row tank resting on 1st row pattern offset)
Mark 2: Dividing by 2: On each side $= 7 \div 2 = 3{,}5 \text{ cm}$
Mark 3: Simplification: $d = 12 - 3{,}5 = 8{,}5 \text{ cm}$
Mark 4: Conclusion: Her statement is VALID.
OR alternative method:
Mark 1: $2d = 1 \text{ tank} + 1 \text{ space} = 12 + 5 = 17 \text{ cm}$
Mark 2: Dividing by 2.
Mark 3: $d = 17 \div 2 = 8{,}5 \text{ cm}$
Mark 4: Conclusion: VALID.
[Award 4 marks]

questions.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix Track and Framed Poster

subQuestions.questionText: The Las Vegas Grand Prix is a 50-lap car race that takes place at the Las Vegas Strip track in Nevada, USA, annually. Identify the shop that a driver will find on his right-hand side at the 13th curve. (Refer to ANNEXURE C in the answer book showing the track layout.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: The Forum
Mark 1–2: Correct shop identified by following the track layout to the 13th curve.
[Award 2 marks for the correct shop]

subQuestions.questionText: State the general direction of the Fountains of Bellagio from the Wynn Golf Club.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: SW (South-West)
Mark 1–2: Correct direction identified using the compass on the track layout.
[Award 2 marks for the correct direction]

subQuestions.questionText: Show, by means of calculations, how the race distance of 310,05 km was determined. (Number of laps = 50; Lap length = 6,201 km.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct value (lap length) – 6,201 km.
Mark 2: Multiplying by 50 laps: $6{,}201 \text{ km} \times 50 = 310{,}05 \text{ km}$
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the road that will be crossed after taking the 4th curve.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Flamingo
Mark 1–2: Correct road identified after the 4th curve.
[Award 2 marks for the correct road]

subQuestions.questionText: The scale of the track layout is 1 : 13 500. One of the race car drivers maintained a constant speed of 204 km/h between points A and B, as indicated on the track layout. Calculate, in minutes, the time it took this driver to cover the distance. Use the formula: Distance = speed × time
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Map distance = 69 mm (Accept measurement from 67 mm to 71 mm; allow ±1 mm deviation from province measurement).
Mark 2: Multiply by scale: $69 \text{ mm} \times 13\,500 = 931\,500 \text{ mm}$
Mark 3: Convert to km: $931\,500 \text{ mm} = 0{,}9315 \text{ km}$
Mark 4: Substitute correct values: $0{,}9315 \text{ km} = 204 \text{ km/h} \times \text{Time}$
Mark 5: Changing subject: $\text{Time} = \dfrac{0{,}9315}{204}$
Mark 6: Simplification: $= 0{,}004566176 \text{ h}$
Mark 7: Convert to minutes: $0{,}004566176 \times 60 = 0{,}2740 \text{ min}$ (approximately).
[NPR]
[Award 7 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Maps and Plans – Scale and Time

subQuestions.questionText: A race car driver decides to practise on the track late in the afternoon. He complained that the rays of the sun were affecting his vision after the 9th corner. State, giving a reason, why you would agree or disagree with this race car driver.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Agree
Mark 1: Agreeing with the driver.
Mark 2–3: Correct explanation – After the 9th corner he will be facing West, and that is the direction in which the sun sets in the late afternoon, so the sun's rays would affect his vision.
[Award 3 marks: 1 for agreeing, 2 for the correct explanation]
subQuestions.topic: Maps and Plans – Direction and Real-Life Application

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 6 shows the fastest laps of the top five race car drivers, including DRIVER, LAP, EXACT TIME OF DAY, LAP-TIME, and AVERAGE SPEED. Lap time 1:35,490 = 1 minute 35,490 seconds. The exact time of day shows the time the driver finished his fastest lap. Calculate, to TWO decimal places, at what time Oscar Piastri started lap 47. (Oscar Piastri: Exact time of day = 23:28:54; Lap-time = 1:35,490.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct value – Exact time of day: $23{:}28{:}54$
Mark 2: Correct value – Lap-time: $00{:}01{:}35{,}490$
Mark 3: Simplification: Start time $= 23{:}28{:}54 - 00{:}01{:}35{,}490 = 23{:}27{:}18{,}51$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Max Verstappen won the race with a time of 1 hour 29 minutes and 8,289 seconds. One of the spectators said Max Verstappen took 5 348,289 seconds, with an average lap-time of 106 seconds, to complete the race. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Converting hours to seconds: $1 \times 60 \times 60 = 3\,600$ s
Mark 2: Minutes to seconds: $29 \times 60 = 1\,740$ s
Mark 3: Simplification: Total seconds $= 3\,600 + 1\,740 + 8{,}289 = 5\,348{,}289$ s ✓
Mark 4: Divide by 50 laps: $\text{Average lap-time} = 5\,348{,}289 \div 50$
Mark 5: Simplification: $\approx 106{,}97$ seconds
Mark 6: Conclusion: Statement is INVALID (the total seconds is correct, but the average lap-time is approximately 106,97 seconds, not 106 seconds).
OR alternative method:
Total time = Average × number of laps = $106 \times 50 = 5\,300$ s = 1 hour 28 min 20 sec
This does not equal the actual time (1 h 29 min 8,289 s), confirming the statement is INVALID.
[Award 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Thabiso wants to buy a framed poster of the Grand Prix world champions. The frame is made up of four pieces of wood joined together with overlaps. Dimensions: Long piece is 630 mm by 45 mm; Short piece is 420 mm by 45 mm; Overlap is 2,5 cm throughout. The frame has two horizontal pieces of wood mounted across two vertical pieces of wood with overlaps. Calculate, in mm, the inner length and the inner width of the frame.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Conversion: $2{,}5 \text{ cm} = 25 \text{ mm}$
Mark 2: Correct value – width of wood: 45 mm.
Mark 3: Subtracting from length: Inner length $= 630 - 2(25 + 45)$
Mark 4: Inside length: $= 630 - 140 = 490 \text{ mm}$
Mark 5: Subtracting from width: Inner width $= 420 - 2(25 + 45) = 420 - 140$
Mark 6: Simplification: Inner width $= 280 \text{ mm}$
[Award 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The poster of the Grand Prix world champions is 485 mm by 270 mm. The person responsible for placing the poster of the Grand Prix world champions inside the frame, stated that the poster will not fit exactly within the frame. Verify, with calculations, whether his statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Q 5.3.1 (Inner length = 490 mm, Inner width = 280 mm).
Mark 1: Subtracting lengthwise: $490 \text{ mm} - 485 \text{ mm} = 5 \text{ mm}$
Mark 2: Simplification: There is a 5 mm gap lengthwise.
Mark 3: Conclusion: Statement is VALID (the poster does not fit exactly – there is extra space).
OR widthwise:
Mark 1: $280 - 270 = 10 \text{ mm}$
Mark 2: Simplification: 10 mm gap widthwise.
Mark 3: Conclusion: VALID.
[Award 3 marks]
